title: The Holy Roman Empire
objective: After this level you can explain what the Holy Roman Empire was, and what it was not.
summary: Often dated from Otto I's crowning in 962 to 1806, the Holy Roman Empire had elected German emperors and became a loose federation. Voltaire mocked it as neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire.

cards.headline: “Neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire.” That was Voltaire’s verdict.
cards.body: The French writer Voltaire aimed that line at the Holy Roman Empire in 1756. Was he fair? Test the name one word at a time.

cards.headline: An emperor crowned in Rome
cards.body: The story usually starts in 962, when the German king Otto I was crowned emperor in Rome by Pope John XII. The name grew slowly: “Holy” joined it in 1157, and the full “Holy Roman Empire” was in use from 1254. It lasted until 1806, when Francis II gave up the title after Napoleon’s rise. More than eight centuries, give or take a word.

cards.headline: Roman? Remember Level 4
cards.body: Start with “Roman”. Its emperors were German kings like Otto, crowned in Rome. Meanwhile, as Level 4 showed, the Byzantines in Constantinople called themselves Romaioi, Romans, and their empire was the eastern half of the Roman Empire itself. Two empires, one Roman name. Voltaire had a point.

mascot.line: Two empires both calling themselves Roman. Somebody should have checked the label.

cards.headline: An empire? Ask the electors
cards.body: Now “empire”. The emperor wasn’t simply born to the job; he was elected. The Golden Bull of 1356 fixed the electors at seven: the archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier, and the rulers of Bohemia, the Palatinate, Saxony and Brandenburg. By the 16th century the empire had become a loose federation. Less a single empire, more a club whose members chose their chairman.

cards.headline: The Holy Roman Empire: known
learned: Often dated from Otto I’s crowning in 962 to 1806
The Golden Bull (1356) fixed seven electors
Voltaire: neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire

questions.prompt: Who wrote in 1756 that the Holy Roman Empire was “neither holy, nor Roman, nor an empire”?

options.label: Otto I
options.rationale: He was its first emperor, not its critic.

questions.explanation: The French writer Voltaire aimed the line at the empire in 1756.

questions.prompt: After the Golden Bull of 1356, how did a man become Holy Roman Emperor?

options.label: He inherited it from his father automatically
He was chosen by seven electors
He won a vote of every town in the empire

questions.explanation: The Golden Bull fixed the electors at seven: three archbishops and four lay rulers.

questions.prompt: Voltaire said the Holy Roman Empire wasn’t Roman. Which empire’s people called themselves Romaioi, Romans?

options.label: The Frankish kingdom of Clovis in Gaul
options.rationale: The Franks gave France its name, not Rome.

options.label: The Umayyad caliphate, ruled from Damascus
options.rationale: A Muslim empire, not a Roman one.

options.label: The Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of England
options.rationale: They were Germanic kingdoms in England.

options.label: The Byzantine Empire, ruled from Constantinople

questions.explanation: The eastern Roman Empire’s people called themselves Romaioi; “Byzantine” is a later name.
